chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Nahwi narrated from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from the mawla of Hurri ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I make drinks from honey and other things, for they compel me to make them for them.' He said, 'Make it and give it to them, and it is permissible before it becomes intoxicating.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling honey drinks before they become intoxicating?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *al-asl fi al-ashya' al--barā'ah* (the default permissibility of things) regarding food and drink, specifically addressing the common practice of producing honey-based beverages. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits their sale and consumption provided they are not yet *muskir* (intoxicating), highlighting the Shia juristic distinction between the substance itself and its potential to become intoxicating. This ruling supports the concept of *tadarruj* (gradual intoxication), where a drink remains halal until it reaches the threshold of causing intoxication.
